newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia may step in to resolve Bakun pact - PM.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia may step in to resolve Bakun pact - PM.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Thursday the government may have to step in to help resolve the dispute in the Bakun hydroelectric dam contract.
The project's main developer Ekran Bhd and ABB Asea Brown Boveri have been in disagreement over some terms of $5.5 billion pact.
"They have been trying but they can't resolve. The next resort is the government will come in," Mahathir told reporters at a go-kart function.
Mahathir said there was also a remote possibility that the government would have to cancel the contract, if the terms were found to be unfair.
"If the worst comes to worst, and it is not possible to carry on, we may have to break the contract," he said.

"We can adhere to the contract if the terms are fair, but if they are shown to be grossly unfair, then we would have no choice. I do not know if it is grossly unfair or not. We will have to study," he added.
Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing said on Wednesday that the dispute was over terms that allowed the ABB-led consortium to claim cost overruns.

ABB and Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos o Obras (CBPO) co-head the consortium that was awarded the contract for the engineering, procurement and construction of the $6.18 billion dam being built in Sarawak state on Borneo island.
A spokesman for ABB's office in Kuala Lumpur declined to comment on Thursday about the status of the contract. He said ABB and Ekran are meeting next week.
A prior meeting between ABB and Ekran on July 24 failed to resolve the differences, which are threatening to delay the $6.18 billion dam, set to be completed by 2003.
